result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A does more of what the request is about: it turns spacing, font sizes, weights, radii, colors and motion into tokens, with role-based names that components use. It also correctly keeps 12/14 and 18/20 as separate values and explains the 2px shift that merging them would cause. B is leaner and its summary is clearer, but it leaves spacing and font sizes as literals, which fits the request less well. A loses points for an unrequested raw-plus-semantic token layer, for dropping `.btn-danger`'s white text color, and for a confusing note about `border:0`. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer A keeps every computed value identical, derives the secondary button's padding from the border width with calc, and stays lean. Its weak spot is leaving spacing and font sizes as literals, saying they don't repeat, when 10px, 14px and 18px do. Answer B tokenizes much more thoroughly and explains the snapping trade-offs well, but it adds a raw-palette layer and dark-theme framing nobody asked for. B also drops `color:#fff` from `.btn-danger`, which could change a combined `.btn-secondary.btn-danger`, and its note about `border:0` being inherited is wrong.
